metadata.title: Robustness of the Hybrid Extragradient-Proximal Point Algorithm

items.name: Definition 1
items.statement:
Let $\varepsilon \geq 0$, the operator $T^{\varepsilon} \colon H \to \mathcal{P}(H)$ is defined as
\[
T ^ {\varepsilon} (x) = \{v \in H \mid \langle w - v, z - x \rangle \geq - \varepsilon \text {for all} (z, w) \in G (T) \}.
\]
It follows that $T^0 = T$ and for each $x \in H$
\[
T ^ {\varepsilon_ {1}} (x) \subseteq T ^ {\varepsilon_ {2}} (x) \quad \text {if} \quad 0 \leq \varepsilon_ {1} \leq \varepsilon_ {2}.
\]
In particular it holds that
\[
T (x) \subseteq T ^ {\varepsilon} (x) \quad \text {for all} \quad \varepsilon \geq 0.
\]
items.remark: [Foundation: SetValued.Basic] recall SetValuedOperator.graph, SetValuedOperator.IsMaximalMonotone | [Notation: paper $G(T)$ maps to SetValuedOperator.graph]

items.name: Remark 1
items.statement:
Let $f:H\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ be a proper closed convex function. Then $\partial f:H\to\mathcal{P}(H)$ is maximal monotone and for $T=\partial f$, it holds that
\[
\partial_ {\varepsilon} f (x) \subseteq T ^ {\varepsilon} (x) = (\partial f) ^ {\varepsilon} (x)
\]
for any $x \in H$, $\varepsilon \geq 0$. The inclusion is proper in the general case (see Ref. 17 for an example).
items.remark: [Foundation: Analysis.ExtendedRealFunctions] recall IsProper | [Note: the subdifferential and epsilon-subdifferential inclusion are not supplied by this paper]

items.name: Algorithm 2.1 Inexact Hybrid Extragradient-Proximal Algorithm
items.statement:
(i) Initialization. Take $x^0 \in H$, $k = 0$.

(ii) Iterative step. Given $x^{k - 1} \in H$, and $c_k > 0$, take
\[
x ^ {k} \approx x ^ {k - 1} - c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k}
\]
where for some $\tilde{y}^{k}$, the pair $\tilde{y}^{k}$, $\tilde{v}^{k}$ is an approximate solution of the system
\[
v \in T (y)
\]
\[
c _ {k} v + y - x ^ {k - 1} = 0,
\]
in the following sense: for some $\varepsilon_{k} \geq 0$,
\[
\tilde {v} ^ {k} \in T ^ {\varepsilon_ {k}} (\tilde {y} ^ {k}), \tag {11a}
\]
\[
\| c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} + \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| ^ {2} + 2 c _ {k} \varepsilon_ {k} \leq \delta_ {k} + \sigma_ {k} ^ {2} \| \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| ^ {2}, \tag {11b}
\]
\[
\| x ^ {k} - (x ^ {k - 1} - c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k}) \| \leq \alpha_ {k}, \tag {11c}
\]
where $\{c_k\}$, $\{\delta_k\}$, $\{\sigma_k\}$ and $\{\alpha_k\}$ are nonnegative and
\[
\sum \delta_ {k} <   + \infty , \quad \sum \alpha_ {k} <   + \infty . \tag {12a}
\]
\[
0 <   \sigma_ {k} \leq \sigma <   1, \quad c _ {k} \geq c > 0, \tag {12b}
\]
for all k.
items.remark: [Foundation: SetValued.Basic] recall SetValuedOperator.zeros | [Prove hint: formalize the iterate and witnesses as an algorithm structure]

items.name: Auxiliary sequence $z^k$
items.statement:
Define an auxiliary sequence
\[
z ^ {k} := x ^ {k - 1} - c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k}. \tag {15}
\]
Observe that $z^{k}$ corresponds to the “exact” extragradient step.
items.remark: [Prove hint: unfold $z^k$ to rewrite the extragradient residual]

items.name: Lemma 3.1
items.statement:
Let $x^{*} \in H$ be a solution of problem (P). Then, for all $k$,
\[
| | x ^ {*} - x ^ {k - 1} | | ^ {2} - | | x ^ {*} - z ^ {k} | | ^ {2} \geq (1 - \sigma_ {k} ^ {2}) | | \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} | | ^ {2} - \delta_ {k},
\]
items.proof:
Proof. By definition of norm in a Hilbert space we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned} | | x ^ {*} - x ^ {k - 1} | | ^ {2} - | | x ^ {*} - z ^ {k} | | ^ {2} &= | | x ^ {*} - \tilde {y} ^ {k} + (\tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1}) | | ^ {2} \\ - | | x ^ {*} - \tilde {y} ^ {k} + (\tilde {y} ^ {k} - z ^ {k}) | | ^ {2} \\ &= 2 \langle z ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1}, x ^ {*} - \tilde {y} ^ {k} \rangle + | | \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} | | ^ {2} \\ - | | \tilde {y} ^ {k} - z ^ {k} | | ^ {2}. \\ \end{aligned}
\]
On the other hand, as $0 \in T(x^{*})$ and $\tilde{v}^k \in T^{\varepsilon_k}(\tilde{y}^k)$, we have by definition of $T^{\varepsilon_k}$ :
\[
c _ {k} \left\langle 0 - \tilde {v} ^ {k}, x ^ {*} - \tilde {y} ^ {k} \right\rangle \geq - c _ {k} \varepsilon_ {k}.
\]
Combining the expression above with (15), we get
\[
\langle z ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1}, x ^ {*} - \tilde {y} ^ {k} \rangle \geq - c _ {k} \varepsilon_ {k}.
\]
Thus we have
\[
| | x ^ {*} - x ^ {k - 1} | | ^ {2} - | | x ^ {*} - z ^ {k} | | ^ {2} \geq | | \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} | | ^ {2} - | | \tilde {y} ^ {k} - z ^ {k} | | ^ {2} - 2 c _ {k} \varepsilon_ {k}.
\]
Now, the desired result follows from (11). [Indeed, (15) gives $\tilde y^k-z^k=\tilde y^k-x^{k-1}+c_k\tilde v^k$, so (11b) bounds exactly the parenthesized nonnegative quantity in the preceding inequality by $\delta_k+\sigma_k^2\|\tilde y^k-x^{k-1}\|^2$. Substituting this bound and collecting the coefficient of $\|\tilde y^k-x^{k-1}\|^2$ yields $(1-\sigma_k^2)\|\tilde y^k-x^{k-1}\|^2-\delta_k$.] In fact, we have that
\[
| | \tilde {y} ^ {k} - z ^ {k} | | ^ {2} + 2 c _ {k} \varepsilon_ {k} = | | \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} + c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} | | ^ {2} + 2 c _ {k} \varepsilon_ {k} \leq \delta_ {k} + \sigma_ {k} ^ {2} | | \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} | | ^ {2}.
\]
Using the last two inequalities, we gather
\[
\begin{aligned} | | x ^ {*} - x ^ {k - 1} | | ^ {2} - | | x ^ {*} - z ^ {k} | | ^ {2} &\geq | | \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} | | ^ {2} - (| | \tilde {y} ^ {k} - z ^ {k} | | ^ {2} + 2 c _ {k} \varepsilon_ {k}) \\ &\geq \left. \left| \left| \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \right| \right| ^ {2} - \left(\delta_ {k} + \sigma_ {k} ^ {2} \right| \left| \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \right| \right| ^ {2}) \\ &= (1 - \sigma_ {k} ^ {2}) | | \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} | | ^ {2} - \delta_ {k}. \\ \end{aligned}
\]
The proof is complete.
items.remark: [Foundation: Hilbert.Basic] recall norm-square expansion | [Prove hint: use the enlargement inequality at $(x^*,0)$]

items.name: Corollary 3.1
items.statement:
Let $x^{*} \in H$ be a solution of Problem (P). Then, for all $k$
\[
\| x ^ {k} - x ^ {*} \| \leq \alpha_ {k} + \sqrt {\| x ^ {k - 1} - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2} + \delta_ {k}}. \tag {16}
\]
items.proof:
Proof. Using the triangle inequality, (15) and the second condition in (11) we get:
\[
\begin{aligned} \| x ^ {k} - x ^ {*} \| &\leq \| x ^ {k} - z ^ {k} \| + \| z ^ {k} - x ^ {*} \| \\ &\leq \alpha_ {k} + \| z ^ {k} - x ^ {*} \|. \\ \end{aligned}
\]
By Lemma 3.1[Rearranging Lemma 3.1 gives $\|z^k-x^*\|^2\leq\|x^{k-1}-x^*\|^2+\delta_k-(1-\sigma_k^2)\|\tilde y^k-x^{k-1}\|^2$. Its right-hand side is nonnegative because it bounds a squared norm, so taking square roots is legitimate.] 
\[
\begin{aligned} \| z ^ {k} - x ^ {*} \| &\leq \sqrt {\| x ^ {k - 1} - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2} + \delta_ {k} - (1 - \sigma_ {k} ^ {2}) \| \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| ^ {2}} \\ &\leq \sqrt {\| x ^ {k - 1} - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2} + \delta_ {k}}, \\ \end{aligned}
\]
and the desired result follows.
items.remark: [Prove hint: combine the algorithm error bound with Lemma 3.1 and monotonicity of square root]

items.name: Lemma 3.2
items.statement:
Let $\{\alpha_k\}$, $\{\delta_k\}$ and $\{\gamma_k\}$ be sequences of nonnegative scalars such that the following conditions are satisfied:

(i) $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \delta_k < \infty$ and $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \alpha_k < \infty$,  
(ii) $\gamma_{k + 1}\leq \alpha_{k} + \sqrt{\gamma_{k}^{2} + \delta_{k}}$ for all $k\in N$

Then $\{\gamma_k\}$ converges to some $L\in \mathbb{R}_{+}$.
items.proof: Cited from: Polyak, B. T., Introduction to optimization, Optimization Software Inc., Publications Division, New York, New York, 1987.
items.source: Polyak, B. T., Introduction to optimization, Optimization Software Inc., Publications Division, New York, New York, 1987.
items.remark: [Prove hint: compare $\gamma_{k+1}$ with $\gamma_k+\alpha_k+\sqrt{\delta_k}$ and use summability]

items.name: Corollary 3.2
items.statement: For any $x^*$, solution of (P), the sequence $\{ \| x^k - x^* \| \}$ converges to some $L \in \mathbb{R}_+$.
items.proof: Proof. Take $\gamma_{k} := \|x^{k-1} - x^{*}\|$. By Corollary 3.1 and (12), Lemma 3.2 applies. [More precisely, with $\gamma_k=\|x^{k-1}-x^*\|$, (16) reads $\gamma_{k+1}\leq\alpha_k+\sqrt{\gamma_k^2+\delta_k}$; (12a) supplies the two summability hypotheses of Lemma 3.2.] Hence, the conclusion holds.

items.name: Corollary 3.3
items.statement:
Suppose that problem (P) has solutions. Then it holds that

(i) The sequence $\{x^k\}$ is bounded.  
(ii) $\lim_{k\to \infty}\| x^{k - 1} - \tilde{y}^k\| = 0.$  
(iii) $\lim_{k\to \infty}\varepsilon_k = 0.$  
(iv) $\lim_{k\to \infty}\| \tilde{v}^k\| = 0,\lim_{k\to \infty}\| c_k\tilde{v}^k\| = 0.$
items.proof:
Proof. Take $x^{*}$ a solution of problem (P). From Corollary 3.2, it follows that
\[
\lim _ {k \to \infty} \| x ^ {k} - x ^ {*} \| = L \in \mathbb {R} _ {+}. \tag {17}
\]
Hence, item (i) holds. [Indeed, convergence of $\|x^k-x^*\|$ makes this real sequence bounded, and $\|x^k\|\leq\|x^k-x^*\|+\|x^*\|$.] We proceed to prove (ii). By Lemma 3.1 and the fact that $\sigma_{k} \leq \sigma < 1$, we have that
\[
(1 - \sigma^ {2}) \| \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| ^ {2} \leq \| x ^ {k - 1} - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2} - \| z ^ {k} - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2} + \delta_ {k}. \tag {18}
\]
Now, as $\lim_{k\to \infty}\| x^k -z^k\| \leq \lim_{k\to \infty}\alpha_k = 0$, and using also (17) it follows that [The reverse triangle inequality gives $|\|z^k-x^*\|-\|x^k-x^*\||\leq\|z^k-x^k\|\leq\alpha_k$; since a summable nonnegative sequence tends to zero, this proves (19).]
\[
\lim _ {k \to \infty} \| z ^ {k} - x ^ {*} \| = L. \tag {19}
\]
Combining (17), (18), (19), and taking into account that $\lim_{k\to\infty}\delta_k = 0$, we conclude that item (ii) holds. [The right-hand side of (18) tends to $L^2-L^2+0=0$, while $1-\sigma^2>0$, hence the nonnegative squared norm on its left tends to zero.]

Recall that, according to (11),
\[
\| c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} + \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| ^ {2} + 2 c _ {k} \varepsilon_ {k} \leq \delta_ {k} + \sigma_ {k} ^ {2} \| \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| ^ {2}.
\]
Since $\sigma_{k}$ is bounded, using also item (ii) and the nonnegativity of $c_{k}$, we conclude that
\[
\lim _ {k \to \infty} \| c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} + \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| = \lim _ {k \to \infty} c _ {k} \varepsilon_ {k} = 0 \tag {20}
\] [The right-hand side of (11b) tends to zero because $\delta_k\to0$, $\sigma_k\leq\sigma$, and item (ii) holds. Each term on its left is nonnegative, so each tends to zero.]
Since $c_k$ is bounded away from zero, we conclude that item (iii) holds. To prove item (iv), observe that
\[
\| c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} \| \leq \| c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} + \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| + \| \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \|.
\]
Combining this with item (ii) and (20), we obtain that $\lim_{k\to\infty}\|c_{k}\tilde{v}^{k}\|=0$. Using again that $c_{k}$ is bounded away from zero, the first claim of item (iv) follows.
items.remark: [Prove hint: use summable nonnegative sequences tending to zero, then separate the nonnegative terms in (11b)]

items.name: Demiclosedness of the epsilon-enlargement
items.statement: Let $T:H\to\mathcal{P}(H)$ be maximal monotone. If $y_j\rightharpoonup y$, $v_j\to v$ strongly, $\varepsilon_j\to0$, and $v_j\in T^{\varepsilon_j}(y_j)$ for every $j$, then $v\in T(y)$.
items.proof: Cited from: Burachik, R. S.; Sagastizabal, C. A.; and Svaiter, B. F., $\varepsilon$-enlargements of maximal monotone operators: theory and applications, Reformulation: nonsmooth, piecewise smooth, semismooth and smoothing methods (Lausanne, 1997), Kluwer Academic Publishers, Dordrecht, pp. 25-43, 1999.
items.source: Burachik, R. S.; Sagastizabal, C. A.; and Svaiter, B. F. (1999), $\varepsilon$-enlargements of maximal monotone operators: theory and applications.
items.remark: [Foundation: FixedPoint.Algorithms] recall Demiclosed; [Note: this is the enlargement-specific weak-strong closedness statement]

items.name: Opial lemma
items.statement: If $x_j\rightharpoonup x$ in a Hilbert space, then for every $z\ne x$, $\liminf_j\|x_j-z\|>\liminf_j\|x_j-x\|$.
items.proof: Cited from: Opial, Z., Weak convergence of the sequence of successive approximations for nonexpansive mappings, Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society, Vol. 73, pp. 591-597, 1967.
items.source: Opial, Z. (1967), Weak convergence of the sequence of successive approximations for nonexpansive mappings, Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society 73, 591-597.

items.name: Lemma 3.3
items.statement: If the solution set of problem (P) is not empty, then $\{x^{k}\}$ converges weakly to a solution.
items.proof:
Proof. First we claim that any weak cluster point of $\{x^{k}\}$ is a solution of problem (P). Indeed, let $\bar{x}$ be a weak cluster point of $\{x^{k}\}$. By Corollary 3.3(ii), $\bar{x}$ is also a weak cluster point of $\{\tilde{y}^{k}\}$. [To account for the index shift, Corollary 3.3(ii), (20), and $\|x^k-z^k\|\leq\alpha_k$ imply $\|x^k-x^{k-1}\|\leq\alpha_k+\|c_k\tilde v^k\|\to0$ and then $\|\tilde y^{k+1}-x^k\|\to0$. Thus a subsequence of $x^k$ weakly converging to $\bar x$ yields the corresponding weakly convergent subsequence of $\tilde y^{k+1}$.] Hence, there exists a subsequence $\{\tilde{y}^{k_{j}}\}$ converging weakly to $\bar{x}$ :
\[
\tilde {y} ^ {k _ {j}} \xrightarrow {w} \bar {x}.
\]
Observe also that, from Corollary 3.3(iii)-(iv):
\[
\begin{array}{l} \tilde {v} ^ {k _ {j}} \stackrel {{\| \cdot \|}} {{\longrightarrow}} 0, \\ \varepsilon_ {k _ {j}} \rightarrow 0. \\ \end{array}
\]
Since $\tilde{v}^{k_j} \in T^{\varepsilon_{k_j}}(\tilde{y}^{k_j})$, and $T^\varepsilon$ has a demiclosed graph (Ref. 19), it follows that $0 \in T(\bar{x})$. [This is precisely the enlargement demiclosedness theorem: along the chosen subsequence, the arguments converge weakly to $\bar x$, the values converge strongly to $0$, and the enlargement parameters tend to $0$.] In other words, $\bar{x}$ is a solution of (P).

By Corollary 3.3(i), $\{x^k\}$ is bounded. So, it has some weak cluster point, say $\bar{x}$, [A bounded sequence in a Hilbert space has a weakly convergent subsequence.] which by the first part of the proof, is a solution of (P). Now we shall prove that the whole sequence converges weakly to $\bar{x}$. Since $\{x^k\}$ is bounded, it is enough to prove that $\bar{x}$ is the unique weak cluster point. Suppose there exists another weak cluster point $\bar{z} \neq \bar{x}$ of $\{x^k\}$. By the first part of the proof, $\bar{z}$ is a solution of (P). Let $\{x^{k_j}\}$ and $\{x^{k_i}\}$ be two subsequences of $\{x^k\}$ converging weakly to $\bar{x}$ and $\bar{z}$, respectively:
\[
x ^ {k _ {j}} \stackrel {w} {\longrightarrow} \bar {x}, \quad x ^ {k _ {i}} \stackrel {w} {\longrightarrow} \bar {z}.
\]
Using the Opial lemma (Ref. 28) we get
\[
\begin{aligned} \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {j} \| x ^ {k _ {j}} - \bar {z} \| &> \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {j} \| x ^ {k _ {j}} - \bar {x} \|, \\ \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {i} \| x ^ {k _ {i}} - \bar {x} \| &> \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {i} \| x ^ {k _ {i}} - \bar {z} \|. \\ \end{aligned}
\]
Using also Corollary 3.2, we conclude that [For either solution $q\in\{\bar x,\bar z\}$, Corollary 3.2 gives existence of $\lim_k\|x^k-q\|$; hence each displayed subsequential liminf equals the corresponding full-sequence limit.]
\[
\begin{aligned} \lim _ {k} \| x ^ {k} - \bar {z} \| &> \lim _ {k} \| x ^ {k} - \bar {x} \|, \\ \lim _ {k} \| x ^ {k} - \bar {x} \| &> \lim _ {k} \| x ^ {k} - \bar {z} \|, \\ \end{aligned}
\]
which is a contradiction.
items.remark: [Foundation: Hilbert.WeakConvergence] recall bounded_sequence_has_weakly_convergent_subsequence, opial_lemma | [Foundation: FixedPoint.Algorithms] recall Demiclosed | [Note: the required demiclosedness is for epsilon-enlargements]

items.name: Normality operator $N_C$
items.statement: For $A \subset H$ , we denote by $A^{\circ}$ the interior of A. Given a closed and convex set C, we recall that $N_{C}$ , the normality operator associated to the convex set C, is $N_{C}(z) := \{w \in H \mid \langle w, z - u \rangle \geq 0 \quad \forall u \in C\}$ if $z \in C$ , and $\emptyset$ otherwise.
items.remark: [Notation: $A^\circ$ is Set.interior $A$; normal cone sign convention is paper-specific]

items.name: Pointwise sum of set-valued operators
items.statement:
For set-valued operators $A,B:H	o\mathcal{P}(H)$, their pointwise sum is the operator $(A+B):H	o\mathcal{P}(H)$ defined by
\[
(A+B)(x):=\{a+b\mid a\in A(x),\ b\in B(x)\}.
\]
items.remark: [Notation: paper writes $T+N_S$; use the pointwise Minkowski sum of set-valued operators]

items.name: Related operator $U$
items.statement:
Let $S$ be the closed ball with radius $2M$ and center 0,
\[
S := \{x \in H \mid \| x \| \leq 2 M \}.
\]
Define
\[
U := T + N _ {S},
\]
where $N_{S}$ stands for the normality operator associated to S.
items.remark: [Notation: paper $T+N_S$ uses ext_def_1; paper $D(T)$ maps to SetValuedOperator.dom]

items.name: Rockafellar sum maximality theorem
items.statement: Let $T$ be maximal monotone and let $C\subset H$ be nonempty, closed, and convex. If $D(T)\cap C^{\circ}\ne\emptyset$, then $T+N_C$ is maximal monotone.
items.proof: Cited from: Rockafellar, R. T., On the maximality of sums of nonlinear monotone operators, Transactions of the American Mathematical Society, Vol. 149, pp. 75-88, 1970, Theorem 1.
items.source: Rockafellar, R. T. (1970), On the maximality of sums of nonlinear monotone operators, Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 149, 75-88, Theorem 1.
items.remark: [Note: instantiate with the ball $S$ and $z_0\in D(T)\cap S^{\circ}$]

items.name: Surjectivity from bounded domain
items.statement: If $U:H\to\mathcal{P}(H)$ is maximal monotone and $D(U)$ is bounded, then $\operatorname{ran} U=H$. In particular, $U^{-1}(0)\ne\emptyset$.
items.proof: Cited from: Brezis, H., Operateurs maximaux monotones et semi-groupes de contractions dans les espaces de Hilbert, Mathematical Studies, North-Holland, Amsterdam, Vol. 5, 1973.
items.source: Brezis, H. (1973), Operateurs maximaux monotones et semi-groupes de contractions dans les espaces de Hilbert, Mathematical Studies, Vol. 5.
items.remark: [Notation: paper uses $U^{-1}(0)$; Lean uses SetValuedOperator.inverse or SetValuedOperator.zeros]

items.name: Lemma 3.4
items.statement: If the solution set of problem (P) is empty, then $x^{k}$ is unbounded.
items.proof:
Proof. Suppose, for purposes of contradiction, that $T^{-1}(0)=\emptyset$, and that $\{x^{k}\}$ is bounded. Now we claim that $\{\tilde{y}^{k}\}$ is also bounded. Observe that $\|x^{k}-z^{k}\|\leq\alpha_{k}$, and hence, $\{z^{k}\}$ is also bounded. Since $z^{k}=x^{k}-c_{k}\tilde{v}^{k}$, it follows also that $\{c_{k}\tilde{v}^{k}\}$ is bounded. Recall that, according to (11),
\[
\| c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} + \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| ^ {2} + 2 c _ {k} \varepsilon_ {k} \leq \delta_ {k} + \sigma_ {k} ^ {2} \| \tilde {y} ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| ^ {2}.
\]
Define $t_{k} := \|\tilde{y}^{k} - x^{k-1}\|$. Expanding the square in the left hand side of the above inequality, and using Cauchy-Schwartz inequality,
\[
\| c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} \| ^ {2} - 2 \| c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} \| t _ {k} + t _ {k} ^ {2} + 2 c _ {k} \varepsilon_ {k} \leq \delta_ {k} + \sigma_ {k} ^ {2} t _ {k} ^ {2}.
\]
Since $c_{k}\varepsilon_{k}\geq 0$ and $\sigma_{k}\leq \sigma$, we obtain
\[
\| c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} \| ^ {2} - 2 \| c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} \| t _ {k} + t _ {k} ^ {2} \leq \delta_ {k} + \sigma^ {2} t _ {k} ^ {2}.
\]
Rearranging the expression above, we get
\[
(1 - \sigma^ {2}) t _ {k} ^ {2} - 2 \| c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} \| t _ {k} + \| c _ {k} \tilde {v} ^ {k} \| ^ {2} - \delta_ {k} \leq 0.
\]
Since $\{\|c_k\tilde{v}^k\|\}$ and $\{\delta_k\}$ converge to zero, take $d \geq \max_k \|c_k\tilde{v}^k\|$ and $\delta \geq \max_k \delta_k$. Then,
\[
(1 - \sigma^ {2}) t _ {k} ^ {2} - 2 d t _ {k} \leq \delta .
\]
Therefore, $\{t_k\}$ is bounded. [Since $1-\sigma^2>0$, the quadratic inequality implies $t_k\leq(d+\sqrt{d^2+(1-\sigma^2)\delta})/(1-\sigma^2)$. Here $d$ and $\delta$ may be chosen as finite uniform upper bounds because the relevant nonnegative sequences converge to zero.] So $\{\tilde{y}^k\}$ is also bounded.

Our aim now is to define a related operator, say U, such that $U^{-1}(0) \neq \emptyset$, and the sequences $\{x^{k}\}$, $\{\tilde{y}^{k}\}$, $\{\tilde{v}^{k}\}$, and $\{z^{k}\}$ satisfy conditions (11)-(12) of Algorithm 2.1 applied to find a zero of U. In order to define such an operator, take $z_{0}$ in the domain of T, and some M > 0 such that
\[
\begin{array}{l} \| z _ {0} \| <   M, \\ \| x ^ {k} \| <   M, \| \tilde {y} ^ {k} \| <   M, \quad \forall k. \\ \end{array}
\]
Let $S$ be the closed ball with radius $2M$ and center 0,
\[
S := \{x \in H \mid \| x \| \leq 2 M \}.
\]
Define
\[
U := T + N _ {S},
\]
where $N_{S}$ stands for the normality operator associated to S. Observe that $z_{0} \in D(T) \cap S^{\circ}$. Therefore, from Ref. 29, Theorem 1, it follows that U is maximal monotone. Furthermore, U has a bounded domain and hence is onto (see Ref. 30). In particular,
\[
U ^ {- 1} (0) \neq \emptyset .
\] [Because $D(U)\subseteq S$ is bounded, the cited surjectivity theorem yields $0\in\operatorname{ran}U$, which is equivalent to $U^{-1}(0)\ne\emptyset$.]
Observe that for proving that the mentioned sequences satisfy conditions (11)-(12) for finding a zero of $U$, it is enough to check the approximated inclusion $\tilde{v}^k \in U^{\varepsilon_k}(\tilde{y}^k)$ for all $k$. In other words, we must show that $\forall (w,z) \in G(U)$,
\[
\langle w - \tilde {v} ^ {k}, z - \tilde {y} ^ {k} \rangle \geq - \varepsilon^ {k}.
\]
Take $(w,z)\in G(U)$. By definition of $U$,
\[
w = u + \eta ,
\]
for some $u \in T(z)$ and $\eta \in N_S(z)$. Note that $\tilde{v}^k \in T^{\varepsilon_k}(\tilde{y}^k)$ and $\tilde{y}^k \in S^\circ$. Therefore by the definition of normal cone and Definition 1 it follows that
\[
\langle u - \tilde {v} ^ {k}, z - \tilde {y} ^ {k} \rangle \geq - \varepsilon^ {k},
\]
and
\[
\langle \eta , z - \tilde {y} ^ {k} \rangle \geq 0,
\]
for all $k \in N$. Hence by summing this two inequalities we get [Since $w-\tilde v^k=(u-\tilde v^k)+\eta$, bilinearity of the inner product makes the sum of the two displayed lower bounds exactly the required lower bound.]
\[
\langle w - \tilde {v} ^ {k}, z - \tilde {y} ^ {k} \rangle \geq - \varepsilon^ {k},
\]
for all $k \in N$. Since $(z, w)$ is an arbitrary point of the graph of $U$ we conclude that
\[
\tilde {v} ^ {k} \in U ^ {\varepsilon_ {k}} (\tilde {y} ^ {k}),
\]
for each $k\in N$

Now we can apply Lemma 3.3 to the operator U and we get that the sequence $\{x^{k}\}$ is weakly convergent to an element $\bar{x}$ in $U^{-1}(0)$. In other words, $0 \in T(\bar{x}) + N_{S}(\bar{x})$. Since $||x^{k}|| < M$ for all $k \in N$, it holds that $||\bar{x}|| \leq M$. Hence, $\bar{x} \in S^{\circ}$, so it must be $N_{S}(\bar{x}) = \{0\}$. [Indeed, $\|\bar x\|\leq M<2M$ places $\bar x$ in the interior of $S$; a normal vector at an interior point is zero, since the normal-cone inequality can be tested against sufficiently small displacements in both directions.] Therefore $0 \in T(\bar{x})$, which is in contradiction with our assumptions. Thus the sequence $\{x^{k}\}$ is unbounded.
items.remark: [Foundation: SetValued.Basic] recall SetValuedOperator.dom, SetValuedOperator.inverse | [Prove hint: contradiction via $U=T+N_S$, then apply Lemma 3.3 to $U$]

items.name: Theorem 3.1
items.statement: If the solution set of problem (P) is not empty, then $\{x^{k}\}$ converges weakly to a solution. If the solution set of problem (P) is empty, then $\{x^{k}\}$ is unbounded.
items.proof: Clearly, the last two lemmas imply Theorem 3.1. [If $T^{-1}(0)\ne\emptyset$, apply Lemma 3.3; if $T^{-1}(0)=\emptyset$, apply Lemma 3.4. These cases are exhaustive.]
items.remark: [Prove hint: split on whether the zero set is empty and apply Lemmas 3.3 and 3.4]

external_theorems.name: Pointwise sum of set-valued operators
external_theorems.statement:
For set-valued operators $A,B:H	o\mathcal{P}(H)$, their pointwise sum is the operator $(A+B):H	o\mathcal{P}(H)$ defined by
\[
(A+B)(x):=\{a+b\mid a\in A(x),\ b\in B(x)\}.
\]
external_theorems.remark: [Notation: paper writes $T+N_S$; use the pointwise Minkowski sum of set-valued operators]

external_theorems.name: Lemma 3.2
external_theorems.statement:
Let $\{\alpha_k\}$, $\{\delta_k\}$ and $\{\gamma_k\}$ be sequences of nonnegative scalars such that the following conditions are satisfied:

(i) $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \delta_k < \infty$ and $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \alpha_k < \infty$,  
(ii) $\gamma_{k + 1}\leq \alpha_{k} + \sqrt{\gamma_{k}^{2} + \delta_{k}}$ for all $k\in N$

Then $\{\gamma_k\}$ converges to some $L\in \mathbb{R}_{+}$.
external_theorems.proof: Cited from: Polyak, B. T., Introduction to optimization, Optimization Software Inc., Publications Division, New York, New York, 1987.
external_theorems.source: Polyak, B. T., Introduction to optimization, Optimization Software Inc., Publications Division, New York, New York, 1987.
external_theorems.remark: [Prove hint: compare $\gamma_{k+1}$ with $\gamma_k+\alpha_k+\sqrt{\delta_k}$ and use summability]

external_theorems.name: Demiclosedness of the epsilon-enlargement
external_theorems.statement: Let $T:H\to\mathcal{P}(H)$ be maximal monotone. If $y_j\rightharpoonup y$, $v_j\to v$ strongly, $\varepsilon_j\to0$, and $v_j\in T^{\varepsilon_j}(y_j)$ for every $j$, then $v\in T(y)$.
external_theorems.proof: Cited from: Burachik, R. S.; Sagastizabal, C. A.; and Svaiter, B. F., $\varepsilon$-enlargements of maximal monotone operators: theory and applications, Reformulation: nonsmooth, piecewise smooth, semismooth and smoothing methods (Lausanne, 1997), Kluwer Academic Publishers, Dordrecht, pp. 25-43, 1999.
external_theorems.source: Burachik, R. S.; Sagastizabal, C. A.; and Svaiter, B. F. (1999), $\varepsilon$-enlargements of maximal monotone operators: theory and applications.
external_theorems.remark: [Foundation: FixedPoint.Algorithms] recall Demiclosed; [Note: this is the enlargement-specific weak-strong closedness statement]

external_theorems.name: Opial lemma
external_theorems.statement: If $x_j\rightharpoonup x$ in a Hilbert space, then for every $z\ne x$, $\liminf_j\|x_j-z\|>\liminf_j\|x_j-x\|$.
external_theorems.proof: Cited from: Opial, Z., Weak convergence of the sequence of successive approximations for nonexpansive mappings, Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society, Vol. 73, pp. 591-597, 1967.
external_theorems.source: Opial, Z. (1967), Weak convergence of the sequence of successive approximations for nonexpansive mappings, Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society 73, 591-597.

external_theorems.name: Rockafellar sum maximality theorem
external_theorems.statement: Let $T$ be maximal monotone and let $C\subset H$ be nonempty, closed, and convex. If $D(T)\cap C^{\circ}\ne\emptyset$, then $T+N_C$ is maximal monotone.
external_theorems.proof: Cited from: Rockafellar, R. T., On the maximality of sums of nonlinear monotone operators, Transactions of the American Mathematical Society, Vol. 149, pp. 75-88, 1970, Theorem 1.
external_theorems.source: Rockafellar, R. T. (1970), On the maximality of sums of nonlinear monotone operators, Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 149, 75-88, Theorem 1.
external_theorems.remark: [Note: instantiate with the ball $S$ and $z_0\in D(T)\cap S^{\circ}$]

external_theorems.name: Surjectivity from bounded domain
external_theorems.statement: If $U:H\to\mathcal{P}(H)$ is maximal monotone and $D(U)$ is bounded, then $\operatorname{ran} U=H$. In particular, $U^{-1}(0)\ne\emptyset$.
external_theorems.proof: Cited from: Brezis, H., Operateurs maximaux monotones et semi-groupes de contractions dans les espaces de Hilbert, Mathematical Studies, North-Holland, Amsterdam, Vol. 5, 1973.
external_theorems.source: Brezis, H. (1973), Operateurs maximaux monotones et semi-groupes de contractions dans les espaces de Hilbert, Mathematical Studies, Vol. 5.
external_theorems.remark: [Notation: paper uses $U^{-1}(0)$; Lean uses SetValuedOperator.inverse or SetValuedOperator.zeros]
